title: How to Get Found Online: 7 Ways to Win Local Search Before 2027
summary: Local SEO for small businesses is evolving in 2026. Learn how to reset your strategy with better listings, reviews, local content, and AI insights to win more visibility and customers in local search.
body_markdown:
Key Takeaways


##


1. Keep your business information accurate everywhere customers search.
2. Optimize your Google Business Profile for the services and areas you serve.
3. Build a consistent stream of authentic customer reviews.
4. Create useful website content around your services, locations and customer questions.
5. Make your online presence easier for search engines and AI tools to understand.
6. Use social media and local content to create more opportunities for discovery.
7. Track leads and customer actions, not just rankings.


**Want to get found online by more local customers?** Start with the places they already search: Google, Maps, business directories, social platforms, review sites, and AI-powered search tools.


Getting found online isn’t about ranking for one keyword or checking off a list of SEO tasks once a year. It’s about building a consistent online presence that helps search engines, AI tools, and customers understand what your business does, where you serve, and why they should choose you.


And you don’t have to wait until January to make a change.


With a few focused updates, you can improve your online visibility, strengthen your local presence, and put your business in a better position to capture customers before the end of 2026.

## How Do You Get Your Business Found Online?


To get your business found online, make sure your information is accurate across major listings, optimize your Google Business Profile, build authentic reviews, create useful website content, strengthen your local authority, and maintain a consistent presence across search, maps, social media, and AI-powered search.


The goal isn’t to be everywhere.


It’s to make your business easy to understand and easy to trust wherever customers discover you.


Think of it as building one connected online presence:


**Listings tell customers where you are.**


**Your website explains what you do.**


**Reviews show that customers trust you.**


**Social content gives people more ways to discover you.**


**AI and search engines use those signals to better understand your business.**


Here’s how to strengthen each piece before the end of the year.


## 1. Make Your Business Easier to Find Online


Before you worry about advanced SEO tactics, check the basics.


Your business name, address, phone number, website, hours and services should be accurate wherever customers might find you.


That includes:


- Google Business Profile
- Google Maps
- Apple Maps
- Online directories
- Industry-specific directories
- Social media profiles
- Review platforms
- Your website


Inaccurate information can create a frustrating experience for customers and make it harder for search engines to confidently understand your business.


### Start with an online presence audit


Search for your business the way a customer would.


Check:


- Is your phone number correct?
- Are your regular and holiday hours current?
- Is your website URL accurate?
- Is your business category correct?
- Are your services listed?
- Is your address consistent?
- Are outdated or duplicate listings appearing?
- Do your social profiles have current information?
- Are there old business descriptions or photos that need updating?


Fix the obvious problems first.


You don’t need a complicated SEO strategy to benefit from accurate, consistent information.


## 2. Optimize Your Google Business Profile


If you want to get found online by local customers, your[Google Business Profile](https://www.thryv.com/blog/google-business-profile-optimization/) deserves regular attention.


Your profile can appear in Google Search and Maps when customers look for businesses like yours. It’s often one of the first places a potential customer encounters your business.


Make sure your profile includes:


- The right primary business category
- Relevant additional categories
- Current services
- An accurate business description
- Current business hours
- Holiday hours
- Recent photos
- Your website
- Relevant business attributes
- Accurate service-area information, where applicable


Then keep it updated.


Added a new service? Update it.


Changed your hours? Update them.


Completed a great project? Add new photos.


Started serving a new area? Make sure your online information reflects it.


Think of your Business Profile as your digital storefront. You wouldn’t leave an outdated sign on your front door for six months. Your online presence shouldn’t look outdated, either.


### Focus on relevance, not keyword stuffing


Google’s local search results are influenced by factors including relevance, distance and prominence.


You can’t control how far away a customer is searching from, but you can make your business information more relevant and complete.


That means clearly explaining:


**What you do.**


**Where you do it.**


**Who you serve.**


Don’t turn your profile into a list of keywords. Make it useful to an actual customer.


## 3. Build Reviews Into Your Customer Experience


Reviews can help you get found online, but they also help customers decide what to do once they find you.


A[strong review profile](https://www.thryv.com/features/automated-reviews/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=OrganicSocial) can answer an important question for a potential customer:


**“Can I trust this business?”**


The best way to build reviews isn’t to launch a once-a-year campaign.


Build a repeatable process.


**Complete the job → follow up → ask for feedback → make it easy to leave a review → respond.**


For example, after completing a service, send a follow-up message thanking the customer and asking them to share their experience.


Consistency matters more than a sudden burst of reviews.


### Respond to the reviews you already have


Don’t overlook the customers who have already taken the time to leave feedback.


Thank customers for positive reviews.[Respond professionally to concerns.](https://www.thryv.com/features/ai-for-small-businesses/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=OrganicSocial#ai-review-response) When appropriate, explain how you’re addressing an issue.


Your responses aren’t just for the person who left the review.


They’re also for every potential customer reading your profile afterward.


And never buy reviews or offer incentives in ways that violate a platform’s policies. Authentic customer feedback is far more valuable than trying to manufacture a perfect rating.


## 4. Create Website Content That Helps Customers Find You


Your website should make it immediately clear what your business does, where you operate and how customers can work with you.


That means going beyond a homepage filled with broad statements like “trusted local experts.”


[Create useful pages around your actual services and locations](https://www.thryv.com/boosts/brand-boosts/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=OrganicSocial) .


For example, a home services company might create pages for:


- Plumbing repair
- Water heater installation
- Emergency plumbing
- Drain cleaning
- Plumbing services in \[city\]
- Emergency plumbing in \[city\]


Then answer the questions customers have before contacting you.


**How much does it cost?**


**What’s included?**


**How long does it take?**


**Do you serve my area?**


**What should I expect?**


**When should I call a professional?**


Useful answers help customers make decisions while giving search engines more context about your business.

### Create content for people, not just keywords


There’s an important difference between useful local content and keyword stuffing.


Creating dozens of nearly identical city pages isn’t a strong local SEO strategy.


Creating genuinely useful pages for the communities and customers you serve is.


Ask yourself:


**Would this page still be useful if search engines didn’t exist?**


If the answer is yes, you’re probably on the right track.


## 5. Make Your Business Easier for AI Search to Understand


Customers aren’t only using traditional search anymore.


They may ask an AI-powered tool questions such as:


- What’s a good electrician near me for an EV charger?””Who offers emergency HVAC service in my area?””What landscaping companies serve my neighborhood?””What’s the best local option for a small bathroom remodel?”


These searches are often more conversational and specific than traditional keyword searches.


That makes clear, useful information even more important.


### How can you get found in AI search?


Start with the same fundamentals that help customers and traditional search engines understand your business:


- Keep business information consistent.
- Clearly describe your services.
- Identify the locations you serve.
- Answer common customer questions.
- Maintain accurate online listings.
- Build a strong review presence.
- Publish useful, original content.
- Earn legitimate mentions from relevant websites and organizations.


You don’t need to create a completely separate[online presence for AI](https://www.thryv.com/blog/what-is-ai-search/) .


Instead, make the information you already have more accurate, useful, and understandable.


**The better you explain your business, the easier it is for search systems to understand what you can offer a customer.**

## 6. Use Social Media to Create More Local Discovery Opportunities


Google isn’t the only place people discover businesses.


[Customers increasingly use social platforms](https://www.thryv.com/blog/local-search-social-media/) to find recommendations, research services, see examples of a business’s work and decide whether a company feels trustworthy.


That gives small businesses another opportunity to get found online.


Use social content to show:


- Recent projects
- Before-and-after results
- Customer stories
- Helpful tips
- Seasonal services
- Local events
- Community involvement
- Your team
- Behind-the-scenes work
- Answers to common customer questions


And when it makes sense, make the local connection clear.


Instead of posting:


**“Another project completed!”**


Tell people what you actually did, what problem you solved and which community you serve.


You aren’t trying to turn every social post into an SEO page.


You’re giving customers another way to discover your business while reinforcing the information they see elsewhere.


## 7. Build Local Authority Beyond Your Website


Getting found online isn’t only about what you publish yourself.


Search engines can also discover information about your business across the wider web.


Look for legitimate ways to build connections in your community and industry.


For example:


- Join a local business organization.
- Sponsor a relevant community event.
- Partner with complementary businesses.
- Participate in local events.
- Contribute expertise to local publications.
- Get involved with community organizations.
- Claim relevant industry listings.
- Earn mentions from organizations you genuinely work with.


The goal isn’t to collect hundreds of random links.


It’s to build genuine local authority.


If your business is known in your community offline, look for opportunities to make that presence visible online, too.


## Your 90-Day Plan to Get Found Online Before 2027


You don’t need to tackle everything at once.


Use the final months of 2026 to work through your online presence in stages.


### Weeks 1–2: Fix Your Foundation


Start with accuracy.


Audit your:


- Google Business Profile
- Online listings
- Website
- Business hours
- Services
- Contact information
- Social profiles
- Review profiles


Correct outdated information and remove obvious inconsistencies.


### Weeks 3–6: Build Relevance


Next, make sure your online presence clearly explains what you do.


Focus on:


- Improving important service pages
- Creating useful location pages
- Adding FAQs
- Updating business descriptions
- Adding relevant services to your listings
- Creating helpful local content
- Adding internal links between related pages


Prioritize the services and locations that matter most to your business.


### Weeks 7–10: Build Trust


Now focus on reputation and authority.


- Ask recent customers for reviews.
- Respond to existing reviews.
- Publish customer success stories.
- Share recent projects.
- Participate in relevant local events.
- Build relationships with complementary businesses.
- Look for legitimate local media and community opportunities.


### Weeks 11–12: Measure What Changed


Don’t judge your progress only by keyword rankings.


Look at business outcomes such as:


- Website traffic
- Phone calls
- Form submissions
- Direction requests
- Bookings
- New leads
- Review volume
- Top-performing services
- Search visibility


Then ask:


**Which changes created the most customer activity?**


Those are the strategies worth carrying into 2027.

## What Can Hurt Your Online Visibility?


Sometimes getting found online isn’t about doing more.


It’s about[stopping the things that work against you](https://www.thryv.com/blog/small-business-seo-mistakes-to-leave-behind/) .


Avoid:


### Keyword stuffing


Repeating the same phrase unnaturally doesn’t make your content more useful.


### Duplicate location pages


Don’t create nearly identical pages for every city just to capture local keywords. Build location content where you can provide genuinely useful information.


### Buying reviews


Fake or purchased reviews can damage customer trust and violate platform policies.


### Inconsistent business information


If your hours, phone number, services or other important details differ across platforms, update them.


### Thin AI-generated content


AI can help with brainstorming and efficiency, but publishing generic content that doesn’t provide anything useful to customers won’t build a strong online presence.


### Chasing every SEO trend


Search will continue to change.


Your strategy doesn’t need to change every time a new tool or feature appears.


Focus on the fundamentals: accurate information, useful content, strong customer experiences, authentic reviews, and a trustworthy online presence.


## How Long Does It Take to Get Found Online?


There’s no guaranteed timeline for improving online visibility.


Some changes can have an immediate impact on the customer experience, such as correcting your hours or phone number. Other improvements, including building reviews, publishing content, and earning local authority, can take longer to show results.


The important thing is consistency.


Getting found online is a process of building and reinforcing signals over time, not a one-time SEO project.


## Getting Found Online Is an Ongoing Strategy


There’s no single switch you can flip to make your business suddenly appear everywhere customers search.


Getting found online happens when multiple pieces of your presence work together.


Your listings provide accurate information.


Your Google Business Profile helps customers discover you locally.


Your website explains your services.


Your reviews build trust.


Your social content creates additional discovery opportunities.


Your local connections build authority.


And your customer experience makes all of those claims believable.


The businesses that consistently strengthen these signals are better positioned to stay visible as search continues to evolve.
